column1: # Quantum defects from TOPbase (the Opacity Project database), as tabulated by
# A. de Kertanguy, arXiv:1308.1017, Tables A-D. Reached by following the
# citation trail from Theodosiou, Inokuti & Manson, ADNDT 35, 473 (1986),
# which this paper cites as its reference [4] and could not itself be obtained.
# *** THEORY, NOT MEASUREMENT. NOT WITNESSED. ***
# Cross-checked against Theodosiou 1986: TOPbase tracks his HARTREE-SLATER
# CALCULATION, not his experiment column. Mg I s is 1.544 here against HS 1.540
# and experiment 1.60. So these cells cannot raise the witnessed count. What
# they CAN do is serve as a third independent theoretical face (R 1575's
# sudoku) across a full ionisation ladder, which no held source provides.
# "Ionization Number Zi" in the source is the ELECTRON COUNT, not the charge.
# Established by two independent readings: Zi = 1 gives delta ~ 0 (one electron)
# and Zi = 3 for lithium gives 0.3995, which is neutral Li's known s-defect.
#   spectroscopic charge z = Z - Zi + 1
# TWO ANOMALIES FLAGGED, NOT SILENTLY PASSED:
#   O  at Zi=2 gives delta_s 0.307, HIGHER than Zi=3's 0.111 - non-monotone
#      where every other chain falls monotonically toward the one-electron zero.
#   Mg at Zi=9 gives delta_p 0.696, IDENTICAL to its delta_s. Every other row
#      has delta_p < delta_s. Both read as transcription faults in the source.
